Did xAI just kill every voice AI startup, again?

Grok Voice 3.0. Their most intelligent speech-to-speech model yet. And the benchmarks are brutal.

86.9 on the Speech-to-Speech Index. GPT-Live-1: 83.2. Gemini 3.8 Live: 82.6. The highest score ever recorded.

98.5% on speech reasoning. Highest of any model tested.

97.0% on conversational dynamics. 94.8% on task completion. First on both.

1070 Elo on human preference. GPT-Live-1 sits at 1048.

Time to first audio: under a second, at 40% lower latency than the frontier models it beats.

It is not a demo. At SpaceX it resolves 70% of Starlink support calls on its own.

Starlink takes 20,000 support calls a day across languages. Millions more voice conversations run inside Tesla cars, every day.

Pricing: $0.08 per minute of audio. $0.025 per completed task, the lowest in the comparison.

Live today in the API and the Voice Agent Builder. Existing agents were switched over automatically.

ElevenLabs spent years building a voice AI company. xAI built voice AI for rockets, cars and satellites. Then made it available to everyone as an afterthought.

Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.

I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.

Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. And that we still lack a lot of information and transparency, including full agent traces and that companies need to remain accountable for what their agents do.

It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

We're sending a bunch of Microducks to assess @AnthropicAI! 

Kidding aside, it hasn't been approved yet but in my opinion, it's very important that open-source engineers and scientists are included in these important endeavors for transparency. That's a big part of why @Thom_Wolf is starting the open alignment initiative. We're all in this together!
